title: Midterms Put Trump-Era Crypto Boom and Prediction Markets Under Pressure
excerpt: Crypto stocks fell as much as 32% in October as investors priced a Democratic Congress, a stalled CLARITY Act and tougher scrutiny of prediction markets.
body:
• Crypto-linked stocks fell sharply in October as investors positioned for a possible Democratic takeover of Congress: Coinbase lost 23%, Bullish 32%, Galaxy Digital 30% and Strategy 15%.
  • Prediction markets priced a Democratic House as near certain on Tuesday morning, with Kalshi putting Democratic control of the House at roughly 94% and the Senate at roughly 75%.
  • The CLARITY Act, which would make the CFTC the primary regulator of digital assets, failed a 49-50 Senate procedural vote on September 15 and analysts say it is unlikely to return in 2027 if Democrats gain.
  • For Indian-origin investors holding US crypto stocks or tokens: the near-term risk described by analysts is oversight and investigations, not a ban — and a presidential veto still limits what a Democratic Congress could enact.

The crypto-friendly regulatory environment built under President Donald Trump is being repriced as Americans vote in the midterm elections. Investors are positioning for a possible Democratic takeover of Congress that could bring tighter oversight of digital assets, renewed scrutiny of prediction markets and investigations involving the president and his associates, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Economic Times.

The positioning showed in October's share prices. Coinbase fell 23% in October, Galaxy Digital declined 30% — its worst monthly performance since 2022 — Strategy lost 15% and Bullish lost 32%, the report said. Demand for protection against a 10% decline in Coinbase shares, relative to potential gains, climbed to its highest level since April, and a similar measure for Strategy reached its highest since June. Shares of the companies advanced on Tuesday as voting got under way.

The law that stalled

At the centre of the reassessment is the CLARITY Act, which aims to establish the Commodity Futures Trading Commission as the primary regulator of digital assets. Democrats, alongside some Republicans, blocked its advancement in September; Blockchain Academics reported the measure failed a 49-50 Senate procedural vote on September 15, short of the 60 votes needed.

https://x.com/ETMarkets/status/2117692373396504836

"A change in control of Congress would most likely reset the timetable for the CLARITY Act."

— Christian Davies, Relm Insurance

Clear Street analyst Owen Lau said he does not expect the CLARITY Act to come back in 2027 given the expected midterm outcome, according to The Economic Times report. Others argue party control is not the whole obstacle: the act was already struggling in a Republican-controlled Senate, Ryan Kirkley of Global Settlement Network noted in the Blockchain Academics report.

Oversight, not just legislation

The more immediate effect of a Democratic House may be investigative. A House majority hands Democrats control of committees, with the power to hold hearings and subpoena documents or testimony. Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Maxine Waters asked the Securities and Exchange Commission in April 2025 to preserve records on Trump's World Liberty Financial, and Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on House Oversight, has named Trump family crypto and foreign business dealings an investigative priority, Blockchain Academics reported.

The industry has spent heavily to shape that outcome. Crypto industry groups spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 races this cycle, according to an October 27 Reuters report cited in the same analysis, with Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz among the main financiers of the Fairshake network. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate races are being decided; Republicans entered the vote holding 219 House seats and 53 Senate seats.

Scrutiny is also arriving from events outside politics. The industry faces questions over cybersecurity following the attempted $6.3 billion theft from Binance in October, and Morgan Stanley analyst Michael Cyprys said the incident could invite greater regulatory scrutiny of cybersecurity, custody and customer asset protection, according to The Economic Times report.

Prediction markets in the crosshairs

Prediction markets, which received federal support under Trump, could find expansion harder under a Democratic Congress. Democrats have introduced the STOP Corrupt Bets Act, which would ban contracts on elections, sports, government actions and war, according to legislation announced by Senator Jeff Merkley and reported by Blockchain Academics. The reach would be wide: sports and parlays made up about 84% of Kalshi's volume this year, against 0.5% for elections. Stricter oversight could benefit established exchanges such as CME Group and Cboe Global Markets over newer platforms, The Economic Times report said.

What a flip would not do

A Democratic majority would not by itself reverse the administration's broader crypto approach. Trump could continue supporting the sector and veto legislation restricting his regulators, and agencies are acting under existing authority regardless of Congress: the SEC granted a temporary innovation exemption for onchain trading of tokenised US stocks two days after CLARITY stalled, and on November 3 CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced equity perpetual futures could begin trading on qualifying US-regulated exchanges, Blockchain Academics reported.

Because a Democratic win is largely expected, analysts say the result may already be priced in. For investors, the midterms may mark the start of a longer reassessment of the regulatory outlook for digital finance, with attention gradually shifting toward the 2028 presidential race.
